claims.text: As-cast TiVNbTa is a single-phase BCC, dendritic high-entropy alloy.
Unreinforced TiVNbTa has a yield strength of 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Unreinforced TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 30% strain and 1273 K.
Adding 0.5 vol% Y2O3 through mechanical alloying and hot consolidation will produce an oxide-dispersion-strengthened TiVNbTa alloy.
The intervention will create a fine dispersion of approximately 50–200 nm Y2O3 nanoparticles in the BCC matrix.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain stable and act as immobile obstacles at 1273 K.
The Y2O3 particles will impede dislocation glide and climb through an Orowan-type strengthening mechanism.
Impeded dislocation motion will reduce recovery and creep at elevated temperature.
Reduced recovery and creep will elevate the yield and flow strength of TiVNbTa at 1273 K.
The ODS alloy will achieve a yield strength of at least 500 MPa at 1273 K, approximately 50% above the stated 330 MPa baseline.
The ODS alloy will achieve a compressive strength of at least 650 MPa at 30% strain and 1273 K.
The prediction applies at 1273 K and a strain rate of 1×10^-3 s^-1 under uniaxial compression between W and CuCrZr blocks.
The prediction is not necessarily applicable above 1373 K or under cyclic loading.
The strength improvement depends on achieving a uniform nanoparticle dispersion and maintaining Y2O3 stability at 1273 K.
